paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God knows His people by NAME. He didn't say, "Moses, go guess how many we've got." He said to list "every man by name, one by one" (Numbers 1:2). Six hundred thousand men, and not one of them was just a number in a pile. I've been the forgotten item in the back of a drawer, so believe me when I say that being known by name hits different.

Now look at how God set the whole camp up. Every tribe got a leader to stand with Moses and Aaron (Numbers 1:4). Every man camped "under his own standard" (Numbers 1:52). The Levites got their own job: they were to "camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it, so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel" (Numbers 1:53). Nobody was left without a place, and nobody was stuck doing somebody else's job.

So here's what it means for you, baker. God has a place for you, and He knows your name. That's good news on the days you feel like one more face in the crowd, or one more cookie in a very big batch. And the passage ends with Israel doing "everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses" (Numbers 1:54). So let's keep our ovens ready and our ears open to what He says.
